{{Youmay|the biological condition|[[Death (town)|the town of the same name]]}}
{{Citation}}
{{Quote|It's okay. Don't be afraid to say it—dead, death, the dead. It isn't going to go away, and if we don't face it, we'll just make it bigger than it really is. Can't live without death, can't die without life.|[[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Kal Skirata]]|<ref name="Order66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>}}
[[File:PadmeFuneral-RotS.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The deceased Padmé Amidala is drawn through the streets of Theed in a casket during her funeral.]]
'''Death''' was the cessation of life functions in a biological organism, permanently rendering it unresponsive to any external factors. The term "death" was also sometimes applied to [[Droid/Legends|droids]] damaged beyond repair. [[Sentience/Legends|Sentient]] individuals (and perhaps all living beings), were known to enter a different [[Netherworld of the Force/Legends|plane of existence]] losing their consciousness and individuality. Some Jedi Masters such as [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], however, could become one with [[The Force/Legends|The Force]], and retain their identity after death. Other known practitioners include [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]. It was a necessary and inevitable part of existence.

==Causes of death==
{{Quote|It seems, in your anger, you killed her.|[[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], telling [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] about his [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|wife's]] death|<ref name="RotS">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
[[File:Death_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Death by blaster bolt]]
In most cases, death was caused by the major body parts within an organism simply "breaking down" from age and/or constant use. However, it could also be caused by irreparable damage to the major organs, such as them being ruptured, sliced, [[Blaster/Legends|blasted]], or similarly damaged. Death could also be caused by the loss of bodily fluids, such as [[Blood/Legends|blood]], as they are required to ferry certain nutrients required for life to continue. In most cases this was [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]], however a number of [[Species/Legends|species]] breathed alternate substances ranging from [[Methane/Legends|methane]] to [[cyanogen]]. Suffocation could also bring about death, as it cut off the source of the required gas. If an organism entered an extremely hot or reactive area, their body could easily burn up and disintegrate, causing instant death.

Another cause was from [[cancer]]s and infections, which occurred when dangerous bacteria and microbes took up residence in the host body, killing the flesh in that area, causing [[Wikipedia:Necrosis|necrosis]], and providing stable residence for more bacteria. Death was either caused by the bacteria getting into the bloodstream and causing necrosis in vital areas of the body, or the necrosis could simply spread and grow, literally compressing the vital organs until they ceased to function.

Suicide was the deliberate choice to end one's life. In certain other cases, death might occur if one simply no longer possessed the will to go on living, regardless of physical condition. [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] was one such individual. Though [[Droid/Legends|droids]] could detect no organic damage to her physical body, Amidala passed away following her heartbreak at what had become of her [[Marriage/Legends|husband]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who had started going by the name [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader, a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]].<ref name="Episode III novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>

Finally, death could be brought by the complete annihilation of the body by forces such as experienced by a being inside an exploding [[Starship/Legends|starship]] or on a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] hit by a [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] blast.

==Death and culture==
{{Quote|Death is a natural part of life. Rejoice for those around you who transform into the Force.|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="RotS" />}}
[[File:The_Price_of_Failure_SoR.png|thumb|right|300px|Death by [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] at the hands of Emperor Palpatine]]
Tending to the dead constituted a significant part of culture. In many cultures, the bodies of the dead were [[Burial/Legends|buried]] either under the ground or in tombs, or [[Cremation/Legends|burned]] to ashes during a [[Funeral/Legends|funeral]] ceremony, attended by friends, relatives, and others who wanted to show their respect for the deceased and mourn their loss. The [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] was known to [[Jedi funeral/Legends|cremate]] the bodies of their dead upon funeral pyres.

The attendance of funerals varied depending on the social status and notoriety of the dead individual. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], [[Funeral of Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|the funeral]] of [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker Lars]], a former [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] and later a [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer's]] wife on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], was attended by a handful of friends and relatives: her premarital son [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], her later husband [[Cliegg Lars/Legends|Cliegg Lars]], his son from a previous marriage [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]], as well as [[Beru Whitesun Lars/Legends|Beru Whitesun]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], and the droids [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]].<ref name="AotC">{{Film|II}}</ref> On the other hand, when Padmé Amidala, former [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] and [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], died in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], [[Padmé Amidala's funeral/Legends|her funeral]] was attended by an enormous procession of mourners, including Queen [[Apailana/Legends|Apailana]] of Naboo, [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]] of the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]], and [[Junior Representative/Legends|Representative]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], her successor as Senator of Naboo.<ref name="RotS" />

[[File:Tusken_burial_site.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raider]] burial site on Tatooine]]
The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] honored their deceased officers with a space burial, where the coffin was released from a [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] into the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. These funerals were usually attended by many other Alliance personnel who served with the deceased.

Some cultures, such as the ancient [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], had a tradition to honor their deceased leaders by putting them to rest in spacious, well-decorated tombs or crypts, along with objects that were dear to them when they were alive, or could potentially aid them in afterlife. The [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]] was an expansive collection of tombs belonging to numerous [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]].

In [[Yuuzhan Vong]] society, death was accepted. They believed the manner in which you died was the most important. Those who died an honorable death in battle would bring pride to their [[Domain]], but those beings who died shamefully would bring dishonor.

In [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture, burials for the dead were uncommon, due to the inability for nomads to sustain cemeteries and the impracticality of bringing bodies with them on the move. However, the [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']], leader of the Mandalorian clans, would be given a proper marked burial as a sign of respect, unless they chose otherwise.<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref> Mass graves and cremation were common when a body could be recovered, with the ashes later scattered, and one of the fallen's possessions—often their [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|armor]]—kept in memorial; if a full set of armor couldn't be recovered, it was commonplace to retrieve smaller parts such as helmets, [[Glove/Legends|gloves]], or plates instead. It was also Mandalorian custom to recite the names of loved ones and friends who have passed each night before sleep as a means of keeping their memory alive.<ref name="The Mandalorians: People and Culture">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref>

===Death and law===
{{Main|Speciecide|Death penalty}}
Although death was considered a part of life, there were nonetheless instances where death was not tolerated, namely in the unlawful taking of life such as various forms of murder, including [[speciecide]], the attempted extermination of an entire species. Some sentences given to lawbreakers also included the ending of the criminal's life, which is known as execution. In such factions such as the New Republic this kind of sentence was usually reserved for very serious charges, such as [[Treason/Legends|treason]].<ref name="Solo Command">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref> However, in some cases, particularly the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], executions were often carried out loosely. The Supreme Commander of the Imperial Forces and Dark Lord of the Sith [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] in particular was rather infamous for often executing those under his command for various blunders they made.

==Death and the Force==
[[File:Rahnvision.png|thumb|right|250px|[[Qu Rahn/Legends|Qu Rahn]] appearing in a vision to [[Kyle Katarn]]]]
{{Quote|There is no death; there is the Force.|The [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]]|<ref name="KotOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
While all beings possessed, to some degree, a natural fear of death, as an undesirable and inevitable yet permanent condition, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], guided by the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]], learned to view death not as a tragedy, but merely as a part of the life cycle. The Jedi, viewing themselves as servants of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], were always ready to sacrifice their lives if necessary.

Some [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force users]] were able to survive in spirit form after their physical body died and interact with living beings, as well as other dead [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]]. This phenomenon mostly manifested itself in the form of [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghosts]], something which applied even to the Sith, like [[Marka Ragnos]] and [[Ajunta Pall]] whose spiritual forms lingered in the [[Realspace/Legends|physical world]] for millennia.

[[File:Vaderstrike.png|thumb|left|250px|Obi-Wan Kenobi becomes one with the Force upon his death at the hands of Darth Vader.]]
Several Sith Lords attempted to [[Immortality/Legends|"cheat death"]] in their own ways: [[Darth Andeddu]], as a spirit, used the Force to retain control over his physically dead and decaying body.<ref name="L5">[[Legacy (2006) 5|''Legacy'' (2006) 5]]</ref> [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], also known as Darth Sidious, used a supply of clone bodies, so he could possess a new body after the previous one died.<ref name="DE">[[Dark Empire 2|''Dark Empire'' 2]]</ref> Other Sith have done the same, including [[Darth Sion]], whose decaying body was held together by the dark side and his own hatred,<ref name="KotOR2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> [[Darth Nihilus]], who transferred his consciousness to his armor, [[Tenebrae|Darth Vitiate]], who transferred his consciousness to the bodies of Sith Lords—titled as the [[Emperor's Voice (Sith Empire)|Emperor's Voice]]—in order to rule the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] forever, and [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], whose spirit was imprisoned in the Massassi Temple on Yavin 4. [[Karness Muur]] tried to cheat death by putting his spirit into a [[Muur Talisman|talisman]], until it was destroyed by [[Cade Skywalker]]. [[Darth Krayt]] was able to use [[dark transfer]] to revive himself from death as well as pass Cade Skywalker through death and back to life again. Cade himself, though not a Sith, used his dark transfer ability to bring several others back from death. Perhaps the most complete attempt at achieving physical immortality was the creation of the midichlorian manipulation techniques of [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]]. The ability could be used to revive the dead, regenerate injuries, and could halt the aging of a practitioner, all without the use of any external resources or energy sources.

==Lifespans==
The term 'lifespan' was used in regard to rough estimates of the length of time a healthy organism belonging to a particular species would live before dying of natural causes. Various species had varying lifespans, from under ten years to almost a millennium. Some [[Species/Legends|species]], such as the [[Diathim/Legends|Diathim]] and [[Talortai/Legends|Talortai]], were known to have indefinite lifespans.
Long-lived species included [[Yoda's species/Legends|Yoda's species]], [[Neti/Legends|Netis]], [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]], [[Anzati]], and [[Gen'Dai/Legends|Gen'Dai]].

It was generally recognized that force users often lived longer lifespans than non-force using members of their species. The Human Jedi Master [[Shayoto]] had lived through the [[Gank Massacres]] and [[Vultar Cataclysm]], placing him well over 800 by [[3997 BBY]], while his [[Shayoto's master's master|master's master]] had allegedly lived through both the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]] and the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], over 2000 years, although he was of an unknown species.<ref name="Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 3">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 3]]</ref><ref name="The Essential Chronology real-world book">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref><ref name="Galaxy at War">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref><ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> One force user, the [[near-Human]] [[Jedi Master]] [[Fay]], was noted by [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] to have been alive for "many centuries" and believed by [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to have been unable to die of aging.<ref name="Republic 53">[[Republic 53|''Republic'' 53]]</ref> [[Volfe Karkko]], an [[Anzati]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]], was already considered old for his species when he was discovered for training some time before the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]]. Karkko lived over another thousand years by harvesting the "[[Soup (Anzati)|soup]]" of defeated Jedi and, upon his imprisonment, the visiting Anzati until he was slain by Quinlan Vos in 30 BBY.<ref name="Star Wars 1998 33">[[Star Wars (1998) 33|''Star Wars'' (1998) 33]]</ref><ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 137">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 137|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 137]]</ref> Whether such extended lifespans were common, however, remains uncertain.

By the time of the [[Galactic War]], the technology existed to extend one's lifespan through artificial means such as [[Youth Preservation Treatment]]s.<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> Much later in the decades leading up to the rise of the Empire such technologies as [[telomere genotherapy]] had become widely available, which Darth Plagueis' droid assistant [[11-4D/Legends|11-4D]] had knowledge of.<ref>[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']] (and [[Darth Plagueis (audiobook)|audiobook]])</ref> Rejuvenation therapies capable of extending lifespans into the 150s were known to be available at the [[Aurora Medical Facility]] on [[Obroa-skai/Legends|Obroa-Skai]], while some [[Bakura/Legends|Bakuran]] citizens were known to live to over 160 with their medical technology.<ref name="Millennium Falcon novel">[[Millennium Falcon (novel)|Millenium Falcon]]</ref><ref>''[[The Truce at Bakura]]'' (and [[The Truce at Bakura (abridged audiobook)|audiobook]])</ref> Certain members of the financial elite were also known to use [[organ transplant]]s and other medical technologies to reach over 300.<ref name="Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels">''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''</ref>
